fix_commit.message: Fix some integer overflow problems when handling corrupt hexdb dumps in the shell tool. [forum:/forumpost/82b513b116 | Forum post 82b513b116].
fix_commit.author: dan

findings.title: Integer overflow in readHexDb() leads to wrong-size allocation and out-of-bounds write
findings.message: In `readHexDb()` in `src/shell.c.in`, the database size `n` and page offset `iOffset` are stored as `int`. Two integer overflow paths exist in the pre-fix code: (1) The rounding expression `n = (n+pgsz-1)&~(pgsz-1)` overflows when `n` is close to INT_MAX (e.g., n=2147483647, pgsz=512: addition wraps to a small negative value), causing `sqlite3_malloc()` to allocate a far-too-small buffer while `memset` zeroes only that tiny region. (2) The subsequent `k = iOffset+j` can overflow when a corrupt hexdb specifies a large page offset, producing a negative `k` that bypasses the `k>=0` guard or an incorrect positive `k` that bypasses the `k+16<=n` guard, causing out-of-bounds writes into the under-sized buffer `a`. A crafted hexdb input with a corrupt `size` or `offset` field can trigger a heap-buffer overflow.
findings.suggestion: Use a 64-bit integer type (i64/sqlite3_int64) for the database size `n` (stored as `sz` after rounding), the page offset `iOffset`, and the per-line offset computation. The fix casts `n` to i64 before the addition: `sz = ((i64)n+pgsz-1)&~(pgsz-1)`, changes `iOffset` to `i64`, and computes `i64 iOff = iOffset+j` for the bounds check.

ground_truth.root_cause: Variables `n` (db size), `iOffset` (page base offset), and `k` (computed byte offset) are all declared as `int`. The rounding computation `n = (n+pgsz-1)&~(pgsz-1)` and the offset sum `k = iOffset+j` are performed in 32-bit signed arithmetic without overflow guards, so adversarially chosen values in the hexdb `size` and `offset` fields cause signed integer overflow (undefined behavior in C), corrupting the computed sizes/offsets used for allocation and bounds checking.
